sentence: This project builds a web portal to brain imaging data shared publicly, so machine learning methods can be used to study human brain dynamics.
This project tries to find ways to inhibit an enzyme in the brain that can counteract the rewarding effect of fentanyl.
This project studies how RNA and proteins interact in sensory neurons and whether this causes persistent pain.
This project tests whether combining cell-engineering and antigen-targeting approaches can make immunotherapy for brain tumors safer and more effective.
This project studies a peptide from a heart muscle protein that improves how cardiac muscle relaxes in diastolic heart failure.
This project uses 3D brain organoids grown from stem cells and single-cell sequencing to look for molecular signatures of opioid use disorder.
This project builds a tool that tests many nanoparticles at once in a single animal to see how they deliver genetic material to diseased tissue.
This project studies how a protein that regulates cholesterol affects the immune response against tumors after radiotherapy.
This project improves a technology that tracks motion on the surface and inside of laboratory animals to study how the brain controls movement.
This project studies how membrane protein complexes such as ion channels are assembled in cells and how that process is regulated.
This project tests whether chemokines and social interventions can strengthen the immune response against tumors in patients with non-small cell lung cancer.
This project builds a 3D heart model from patient skin cells to study how Duchenne muscular dystrophy progresses and whether correcting the mutation stops it.
This project provides imaging of living animals, from whole animal fluorescence and bioluminescence to intravital microscopy, to study cancer therapeutics and tumor biology.
This project studies the brain changes caused by alcohol exposure and withdrawal and how those changes can be reversed.
This project develops tests that detect ovarian cancer in uterine lavage samples by measuring proteins and methylation across the genome.
This project studies how perineuronal nets, semaphorin 3A and substance P affect social recognition in mouse models related to autism spectrum disorder.
This project tests how transcranial magnetic stimulation changes electroencephalogram markers in people with cocaine use disorder.
This project builds graph-based models of genetic variation to understand genetic factors behind common diseases like coronary artery disease and Type 2 diabetes.
This project enables imaging of cellular dynamics in ocular tissues and provides a central resource for quantitative image analysis.
This project develops a technology called cellular self-reporting that gets living cells to secrete molecules for analysis without harming the cell.
